name: Latvia
summary: EU citizens register their residence. Non-EU nationals lost the property and bank-deposit residence routes when the new Immigration Law took effect on 15 September 2026; the remaining investor route is EUR 50,000 (EUR 100,000 for larger firms) in a Latvian company's share capital plus a EUR 10,000 state payment, and a EUR 150,000 fund route that is not operational yet. Russian and Belarusian citizens are barred from investor permits. A remote-work visa exists but its income threshold is unverified.
naturalisation: Reported as 10 years of legal residence, the last 5 on a permanent residence permit, with Latvian language (A2) and history/constitution tests and legal income. The 10-year figure comes from secondary guides; an official PMLP brochure speaks only of 5 years of permanent residence. Not verified against the Citizenship Law.
dual_citizenship_note: Dual citizenship is allowed on naturalisation for citizens of EU, EFTA and NATO states and some others; other nationalities may be asked to renounce (secondary sources, not verified against the law).

routes.name: EU/EEA free movement
routes.summary: EU citizens register their residence after three months; no investment or permit needed.
routes.requirements: Directive 2004/38/EC: register with PMLP for stays over 3 months; permanent residence after 5 years of continuous residence.

routes.name: Temporary residence permit: investment in company share capital
routes.summary: Residence for investing in the share capital of a Latvian company, with a required state payment and tax contributions.
routes.requirements: Small firm (up to 50 employees, turnover or balance sheet up to EUR 10 million): EUR 50,000 investment, a EUR 10,000 payment to the state at the first permit and at least EUR 40,000 yearly tax payments by the company. Larger firm: EUR 100,000 investment and EUR 100,000 yearly taxes. Permit now up to 2 years (previously 5). Russian and Belarusian citizens excluded. Figures from secondary sources on the new law effective 15 September 2026; not checked against the official text.
routes.physical_presence: Not sourced; investor must maintain the company and permit conditions

routes.fees_note: EUR 10,000 state payment at first permit (secondary sources); ordinary state fees extra, not sourced.
routes.tax_note: A residence permit does not make you tax resident (183 days in 12 months or declared residence does).

routes.name: Temporary residence permit: state-established alternative investment fund
routes.summary: New EUR 150,000 route via a state-established fund, with a 5-year hold. The fund did not exist yet.
routes.requirements: EUR 150,000 held for at least 5 years plus a EUR 10,000 state payment; permit up to 5 years. OCMA reportedly confirmed that the state fund has not been created, so no application can be made. Russian and Belarusian citizens excluded.

routes.status_note: Introduced by the new Immigration Law effective 15 September 2026; not operational as of the sources found (state fund not yet created).

routes.name: Temporary residence permit via real estate (old route)
routes.summary: Residence for buying property worth EUR 250,000 or more; closed to new applications on 15 September 2026.
routes.requirements: Old rule: property of at least EUR 250,000 (Riga, Jurmala and listed areas: one property; elsewhere up to two), cadastral value at least EUR 80,000, paid non-cash, plus 5% of the price to the state budget (EUR 12,500 at the minimum). Subsistence proof EUR 1,500 a month. Applications lodged by 14 September 2026 are decided under the old law (5-year permit).

routes.status_note: Not available to applications from 15 September 2026 under the new Immigration Law; applications filed up to 14 September 2026 are still assessed under the old rules.
routes.fees_note: 5% of the purchase value paid to the state budget at the first application (EUR 12,500 on EUR 250,000); other state fees not sourced.
routes.tax_note: Does not by itself make you tax resident.

routes.name: Temporary residence permit via bank deposit (old route)
routes.summary: Residence for a EUR 280,000 subordinated deposit with a Latvian bank; closed on 15 September 2026.
routes.requirements: Secondary sources say the EUR 280,000 deposit route is not retained in the new Immigration Law. Original conditions not re-verified.

routes.status_note: Dropped from new applications from 15 September 2026; applications filed by 14 September 2026 follow the old rules.

routes.name: Remote worker (digital nomad) visa
routes.summary: Long-stay visa for non-EU remote workers employed by or registered in a foreign (reported OECD) company; the income threshold is unconfirmed.
routes.requirements: Reported minimum monthly income varies between EUR 3,192.50 and about EUR 4,213 across sources; no PMLP page was retrieved. Up to one year; no local employment.
routes.tax_note: No special tax regime; tax residence applies after 183 days.

routes.name: EU Blue Card and employment permits (work)
routes.requirements: Threshold for the Blue Card not confirmed for 2026 (one table reports about EUR 32,676 a year, undated). Job offer of at least 6 months and a degree needed.

open_questions: New Immigration Law: official text and effective date (Latvijas Vestnesis / OCMA) not retrieved; all details are from law-firm and news sites. One consultancy gave 1 January 2027 for some provisions.
Whether the investor company route permit is two years and whether it leads to permanent residence; years to permanent residence for investors.
Remote-worker visa: official PMLP income threshold, fee and renewability.
EU Blue Card salary threshold for 2026 and fees.
Naturalisation: 10 years (last 5 permanent) versus PMLP brochure's 5 years; dual citizenship rules by nationality.
Latvia has no passive-income permit found; confirm none exists under the new law.
